main_text.p: non sunt, sed ad rusticis sudoribus iniuriam inferendam paratissimæ.
main_text.head: Amat. CHRYSIPPA SOSIPATRO. LXXXIV.
main_text.p: Amatoriis retibus nónne captus es, Sofipater, qui Anthusam ames? ingenuorum oculorum fignum est, adolescentulam amare decoram, ne ingemisce victus pulcritudine. maius enim oblecta mentum inde capies. Amatoriæ lacrimæ, dulces exiftunt. nam voluptate sunt commissæ, quæ dolorem alias creant. & exhilarant Amores, cum trifta uerint. multiplicibus enim affectibus veneris cestus est insculptus.
main_text.head: Eth. PLATO DIONYSIO. LXXXV.
main_text.p: Si mœrorem vis vincere, circui sepulchra. & passionis inuenies remedium, & maximas hominum fortunas vlterius cinerem videbis esse nihil.

page.notes: The "FINIS" line is set in spaced capitals with an italic/decorative style, so it is given as a foot line. The heading lines "Amat." and "Eth." are italic abbreviations of the speaker/topic. Several words in the text show the printer's own spelling (e.g. "ingemisce", "uerbum"-type forms). Faint marks in the lower part of the page are stains or show-through and were not transcribed. Some words in the first paragraph of the second letter ("cinerem") are read from the scan with moderate confidence; the word "trifta uerint" is copied as printed.
